mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered 6.3 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w (−31.3 to −25.0), signaling renewed commuting and urban circulation. This sustained recovery in transit access over the next four weeks will drive retail-and-recreation footfall upward as workers and visitors return to commercial districts.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.3 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or TRANSIT mobility declines more than 5 points in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 8.3% to 5.1% over four weeks, indicating residents are spending less time at home. This behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity will manifest as increased retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks as the trend continues.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.2 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 6.0% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered 7.4 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w (−44.7 to −37.3), indicating return-to-office momentum. When workplace attendance crosses above −35% in the next week, retail-and-recreation mobility will increase as office workers resume lunch, shopping, and after-work leisure patterns.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above −35% in any single week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not sustain above −35% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines in the week following the trigger event.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has improved 5.5 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w (−24.1 to −18.6), while RETAIL_REC has improved 3.8 points. The co-movement of essential and discretionary retail signals a broader reopening dynamic. When both series move in the same direction over the next two weeks, retail-and-recreation will accelerate upward.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both improve week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC diverge in direction in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around 6–9% above baseline over four weeks, indicating sustained outdoor activity preference. In early autumn (mid-September), this outdoor-activity baseline will compete with retail-and-recreation visits. If PARKS mobility remains elevated above 8%, retail-and-recreation will remain suppressed below its baseline recovery trajectory.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 8% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below 5% in any week, or RETAIL_REC rises more than 5 points above its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility are both severely depressed (−25.0% and −37.3% respectively at t-0w), suggesting ongoing capacity restrictions or voluntary avoidance. If both remain below their t-3w levels over the next four weeks, retail-and-recreation will remain suppressed as the urban mobility ecosystem fails to recover.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below t-3w levels for all four weeks
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above t-3w levels in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases more than 3 points from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 3.8 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w (−37.7 to −33.9), the largest single-week gain in the four-week window. This momentum signal, combined with GROCERY_PHARM improvement and TRANSIT recovery, indicates a coordinated shift in mobility behavior. The interaction of these three signals will sustain and amplify retail-and-recreation growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: all three series improve week-on-week at the decision point
failure_condition: Any of the three series declines in the first week following the decision point, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed −30% by week 2.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered 7.4 points from t-1w to t-0w but remains at −37.3%, indicating incomplete return-to-office. RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined to 5.1%, the lowest in the four-week window. This divergence—workers not returning to offices while leaving homes—suggests displacement to alternative venues. Retail-and-recreation will decline as workers remain in hybrid or remote arrangements without compensatory leisure mobility.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below −35% while RESIDENTIAL stays below 6%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at −37.3% and RESIDENTIAL at 5.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above −30% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases more than 4 points from t-0w baseline.
